question: The Commission has stated to Parliament that Israeli beneficiaries of Horizon Europe cannot be considered in breach of Article 14 of the Horizon Europe Model Grant Agreement merely because they are established in Israel and that measures must be based on the beneficiary’s conduct rather than on the actions of the State of Israel1.

Previously, however, the Commission proposed a partial suspension of the Horizon Europe Partnership Agreement based on Israeli violations of Articles 2 and 79(2) of the EU-Israel Association Agreement.

Under such a suspension, legal entities established in Israel, irrespective of their individual conduct, would no longer be eligible to participate in Horizon Europe calls linked to the EIC Accelerator funding programme. While more limited, the latter proposal aligns better with the Commission’s March 2022 general suspension of cooperation with Russian beneficiaries2. 1.

Does the Commission confirm that legal consequences may be imposed on Israeli entities based on conduct attributable to the State of Israel, provided that the legal basis is the violation of Article 2 of the Association Agreement?
If so, why has the Commission shifted back to presenting the issue as one of beneficiary conduct rather than one of restrictions resulting from the conditions of an international agreement?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.10.2026) 1. While the Commission recognises the breach of human rights by the State of Israel, the Commission stands by its position that actions or behaviour of the State of Israel cannot be considered automatically attributable to Israeli entities participating in Horizon Europe grants.

As long as the agreement1 associating Israel to Horizon Europe remains fully applicable, Israeli entities remain eligible to participate on this basis and any termination based solely on nationality grounds would amount to discrimination prohibited under this agreement.

Notwithstanding, any established breach of the applicable Horizon Europe rules by a particular entity may give rise to any of the contractual measures as foreseen in the Horizon Europe model grant agreement that are to be determined taking due account of the seriousness of the breach and their proportionality towards addressing this. 2.

In proposing the partial suspension of the agreement associating Israel to Horizon Europe2, the Commission responded to the breach by the State of Israel of its obligations under Article 2 of the Euro-Mediterranean Agreement3 in a way considered to be proportionate.
In particular, in line with its Article 79, stating ‘In the selection of measures, priority shall be given to those which least disturb the functioning of the Agreement’.

As a consequence of the breach by the State of Israel of its obligations under Article 2 of the Euro-Mediterranean Agreement, the Commission has also proposed sanctions on extremist ministers of the Israeli government and a suspension of trade concessions with Israel, while halting bilateral support.
